_note: Seed values (version = when prices changed; a change recomputes the usage ratios). price = relative price of each token type against one input token of the same model; the cache read depends on the model (Haiku 0.1; Sonnet and Opus 0.05; Fable 0.025). model_weight = the model's input price against Opus 5.5 (API list, 2026-10-12: Haiku 5.5 $0.10, Sonnet 5.5 $2, Opus 5.5 $4, Fable 5.1 $10 per million). long_prompt = Haiku 5.5 bills a request whose prompt (input + cache reads + cache writes) is over 100,000 tokens at 5x every price; the other models have one price up to 1M; usd_per_mu = dollars one million u costs. roles: default model and effort (the starting point Anthropic recommends for each model: Opus 5.5 at medium, agentic Sonnet 5.5 at medium/high, Haiku 5.5 at low for mechanical work; all three take low-max) and the SHAPE of one agent of that role (turns, average context per turn, i.e. what it re-reads from cache every turn, and output tokens at the given effort), measured on real workflows in 2026-09: reviewers and searchers with tools ~25 turns at ~100k context; verifiers that get everything in their prompt ~4 turns at ~40k; trivial Haiku agents 2 turns, ~15k, ~300 output; implementers (implement) a median of 55 turns at ~135k and ~10k output, and correctors that apply given findings (fix) 16 turns at ~96k and ~1.5k output (30 samples, 2026-10). The cache write is approximated as ctx x (0.5 + 0.05 x turns). effort_output and effort_turns = how much output and turns change with effort (Anthropic measures per task: medium 70-87 % of the cost, low 33-50 %). seconds_per_turn = wall-clock seconds per turn of each model, measured on the same workflows. runaway_factor = output cap in thorough mode (brake against loops that never converge), light_factor in light and cut_factor in the fine-grained cuts, all over the estimated output. spent_ratio = budget.spent() over the real output of the agents (budget.spent() counts more than the agents' transcripts show; >4.4 measured 2026-10): the cap multiplies by it, and `finish --spent` learns it. `finish` learns the real shape and seconds per turn and replaces the seed.

mechanical.for: search, list, inventory, read and summarise without judgement

extraction.for: pull data into a schema, transform, compare against a given rule

analysis.for: review through one lens, investigate a subsystem, find issues

design.for: design, choose between alternatives, write the deliverable

implement.for: implement a change in a codebase: read, edit, run its tests

fix.for: apply given review findings to an existing change

synthesis.for: final judge, synthesis of the result

light._note: Light mode (less usage and effort): the cheapest model that still does the task, at the lowest effort, one vote and one round; every agent is kept (coverage is never cut). Never raises what the plan set lower.

risk._note: What light mode risks per role when it lowers the model: printed under the light estimate so the user weighs quality, not only cost.
risk.extraction: Haiku slips on schemas and rules more often: check the output
risk.analysis: low effort finds fewer issues per lens
risk.design: Sonnet weighs alternatives less well: review the deliverable
risk.implement: Sonnet on core or engine code needs more correction rounds
risk.fix: Sonnet may apply a finding literally and miss its intent
risk.verify: a Sonnet verifier refutes less: more false findings survive
